priceContext: Coffee C futures remain elevated near multi-month highs amid persistent supply concerns, though profit-taking Friday capped gains ahead of the long weekend.
iceStocksChange: -18,200 bags WoW (-2.2%), lowest level since Q3 2024
usdBrlContext: BRL mildly firmer vs prior week; stronger BRL reduces Brazilian farmer USD incentive to sell, mildly supportive for prices.
summary: Coffee C futures pulled back modestly Friday but hold MTD gains above 4%. ICE certified stocks continue their multi-week drawdown, now at critical lows. Brazil's 2026/27 crop development remains the dominant market narrative with key flowering moisture conditions in focus. Red Sea disruptions persist, elevating freight costs on Vietnam-to-Europe corridors. Risk level stays High given tight stocks, weather uncertainty, and macro FX volatility.
bullish: ICE certified stocks near 18-month lows at 812k bags, structural tightness supporting floor prices
Brazil Minas Gerais and Espirito Santo receiving below-normal rainfall in May; flowering stress risk for 2026/27 Arabica crop
BRL firming to 5.61 reduces Brazilian farmer selling incentive, limiting physical supply flow to market
bearish: Vietnam robusta harvest nearly complete with trade estimates of 28-29 million bags, above prior-year levels
Demand destruction risk rising as retail roaster pass-through prices hit consumer resistance in US and EU
Macro headwinds: Fed holding rates higher for longer, USD broad strength could return and pressure EM currencies
weather: BRAZIL: Minas Gerais and Cerrado regions recording 40-55% of normal rainfall in May; soil moisture deficits building ahead of critical June-July dormancy and pre-flowering period for 2026/27 arabica crop.

VIETNAM: Central Highlands dry season concluding; harvest 95%+ complete. Early monsoon onset forecast for late May providing adequate soil recharge for next cycle. Robusta supply outlook neutral-to-bearish.
EL NINO/LA NINA: ENSO-neutral conditions expected to persist through Q3 2026 per NOAA; tail risk of weak La Nina developing in Q4 which could stress Colombian and Central American production.
freight: Red Sea diversions via Cape of Good Hope remain standard routing for Asia-Europe coffee shipments, adding 10-14 days and $180-240/MT vs pre-crisis norms. Hormuz risk low for coffee lanes but elevated for energy costs affecting reefer fuel surcharges.

news.text: ICE warehouse drawdowns accelerated in May, with certified stocks hitting 812k bags; trade sources cite roaster restocking demand absorbing available certified coffee.
Vietnam's General Statistics Office reported April 2026 coffee exports at 185,000 MT, up 9% YoY, signaling robust robusta availability pressuring NY/London spreads.
Brazil INMET weather service flagged anomalous dryness across key arabica regions; if June rainfall misses forecasts, 2026/27 crop estimates could face downward revisions by July.

changed: ICE certified stocks declined faster than expected this week, moving the inventory outlook from neutral to bearish-for-bears (bullish price signal)
USD/BRL moved from 5.67 to 5.61 this week, reducing Brazilian farmer FX incentive to price and deliver beans

watch.title: Brazil June Rainfall
watch.desc: First two weeks of June rainfall across Minas Gerais and Espirito Santo will be pivotal for 2026/27 flowering prospects; any deficit confirmation likely triggers sharp upside move.

watch.title: ICE Stocks Threshold
watch.desc: If certified stocks break below 800,000 bags, algorithmic and speculative buying could accelerate; watch Tuesday post-holiday warehouse report closely.

watch.title: USD/BRL FX Trend
watch.desc: Further BRL appreciation toward 5.50 would significantly curb Brazilian export flow and tighten spot availability; monitor Brazil central bank communications and US macro data this week.
